newsitem.title: USA: NGC profits plunge on charges in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: NGC profits plunge on charges in first quarter.

text.p: NGC Corp. said Thursday its profits plunged in the first quarter as it took pretax charges of $38.3 million for losses in its natural gas liquids business, to write down crude oil inventories and set up a loss reserve.

The Houston-based gas, electricity and oil company said net income for the quarter ended March 31 sank to $4.6 million, or 3 cents a share, from $30.3 million, or 26 cents a share, in the 1996 period.
Operating revenues almost doubled to $3.27 billion from $1.65 billion.

The latest results include a pretax charge of $20.6 million announced in March for hedging-related losses in NGC's natural gas liquids business and a write-down on the cost of its natural gas liquids inventory.
NGC also took a $2.7 million pretax charge to reduce its crude oil inventories to market prices, and posted a pretax gain of $3.4 million from the sale of a unit in Mont Belvieu.
In addition, the company has established a reserve related to its investment in a storage project of $15.0 million before taxes.
Excluding the charges and gain, NGC's net income for the first quarter was $26.6 million, or 16 cents a share.
NGC had warned in March that its earnings would be far below analysts' forecasts then of 28 cents a share.

"While we are disappointed with the results of the quarter, we are confident about the outlook for all aspects of our businesses for the remainder of the year and beyond," said NGC Chairman and Chief Executive Chuck Watson.

"We have taken the necessary steps to assure that our business processes and systems function properly in light of the more complex business activities that have resulted from our explosive growth over the past two years."
NGC said it has continued to strengthen its senior management team and shifted certain responsibilities to ensure that the problems in the first quarter are no longer a risk.
"In short, NGC's rapid growth has created an entirely different company than what existed just two years ago, and our charge now is to manage -- yet continue -- that growth," Watson said.

NGC is a leading gatherer, processor, transporter and marketer of energy products and services in North America and Britain. Through its "Energy Store," NGC provides natural gas, natural gas liquids, electricity and crude oil.
